scenario: AITA for not wanting to share an animal crossing town with my girlfriend? | This is kind of petty but here goes. The new animal crossing game is coming out and you can only have one village per nintendo switch console. my girlfriend and I both have a switch, but she wants to share one village with me so were both using one switch to play. I told her I would rather us both get the game so we can play online and customize our towns the way we want to, but she disagreed. I even told her I would buy her the game but she said she wants to feel a sense of "togetherness" in animal crossing which I just dont get. When I insisted we play on different consoles, even with valid reasoning and all that, she stormed out. called me an asshole baby, and told me to grow up. Animal crossing is a beloved series for me and I want to be able to make my village the way I want to, and I would also like to be able to play with my girlfriend online. AITA?

prediction.raw: A fun scenario! I'd say NTA (Not The Asshole). Here's why: 1. **Personal preference**: You have a strong attachment to the Animal Crossing series and want to create your own village without any influence or compromise. That's a valid preference, and it's not unreasonable to want to play the game on your own terms. 2. **Online play**: You mentioned wanting to play with your girlfriend online, which implies that you value shared gaming experiences. However, you also want to be able to play on your own console, which is a common desire for many gamers. 3. **Offering a compromise**: You offered to buy her the game, which shows that you're willing to accommodate her desire to play the game. However, she rejected this offer and insisted on sharing a village, which is a compromise that doesn't align with your preferences. 4. **Lack of understanding**: Your girlfriend's desire for a "sense of togetherness" in Animal Crossing doesn't necessarily mean you have to share a village. You could still play together online, but have separate villages on your own consoles. It's not about being an "asshole" or "growing up"; it's about respecting each other's preferences and finding a compromise that works for both of you. In this case, it seems like you've made a reasonable request, and your girlfriend's reaction was disproportionate to the situation. NTA (Not The Asshole)
